prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Conservatives argue Britain is a great country held back by the wrong values and waste under Labour. It’s time for action, not talk: reward people who work hard, pay their taxes, play by the rules; restore discipline, security and choice; devolve power; and focus government on practical priorities—cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes. A Conservative government will govern for everyone, with equal treatment and accountability at its core.

- Value for money and lower taxes: Cut £12bn of waste by 2007–08 (fewer bureaucrats, axed quangos) to reduce borrowing (£8bn) and fund tax cuts (£4bn). Increase spending more slowly than Labour, but match/raise funding for NHS, schools, police, defence and pensions. Halve council tax for millions of pensioners; restore the basic state pension’s link to earnings; keep pensioner benefits. Encourage saving via Lifetime Savings Accounts; strengthen workplace pensions. Keep the pound, keep Bank of England independence, restore a pro-enterprise, deregulated economy and resist EU job-destroying rules.

- Families, childcare, schools: Trust parents with flexible childcare support (up to £50/week per under‑5 via tax credits), flexible maternity pay, more workplace nurseries and clubs. Restore discipline: give heads control over expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; protect teachers from malicious allegations and paperwork. Money follows the pupil; schools free to innovate; restore exam rigour and transparency; allow respected international qualifications. Boost vocational routes (300,000 grants). Two hours after-school sport and ban junk food. Expand parental choice (600,000 new places; allow state funding for low‑cost independent places). Moratorium on special school closures. Scrap university tuition fees and Labour’s admissions regulator; help build endowments.

- NHS and social care: More funding (to £2,000 per head), less bureaucracy (abolish SHAs, slim PCTs, scrap central targets). Empower local professionals; bring back Matron; fund follows the patient; protect community hospitals; support GP choice. End waiting lists as we know them; part‑fund private operations to cut queues. Partnership on long‑term care so no one must sell their home; better support for carers; fix NHS dentistry. Health checks for long‑term migrants; robust STI public health campaign.

- Law and order: 5,000 extra police annually; slash paperwork; elected police commissioners; zero-tolerance neighbourhood policing. End early release; 20,000 extra prison places; honesty in sentencing. Expand rehab (25,000 residential places); reverse cannabis to Class B. Appoint a Homeland Security Minister.

- Controlled immigration: Welcome contributors, but restore control. 24/7 port surveillance; British Border Control Police; restore embarkation checks. Australian‑style points system. Set an annual limit, including a UNHCR refugee quota. Process asylum outside the UK; repatriate powers from Brussels; update international rules.

- Accountability and the constitution: Ministers who fail go. Publish a Timetable for Action. Abolish regional assemblies; return powers to local councils; strengthen Parliament and select committees; cut MPs by 20%; pursue a substantially elected Lords. English votes for English laws. Support the Union; firm principles for Northern Ireland.

- Communities, housing, transport, environment: Devolve planning; act against illegal traveller camps; extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership. End Labour’s war on motorists; modernise roads; review speed cameras; longer rail franchises. Protect the Green Belt; prioritise brownfield; phase out HFCs; incentivise low‑emission cars; boost recycling and energy efficiency; ensure energy security with diverse renewables. Support farmers: honest food labelling, Little Red Tractor for public procurement, cut red tape, reform CAP. Free vote to overturn the hunting ban; strengthen animal welfare.

- Britain in the world: Spend more on the Armed Forces’ front line; support service families; preserve regiments and key warships; keep NATO central. Be honest about war; stay committed to rebuilding Iraq and a two‑state solution in the Middle East. Say no to the Euro and the EU Constitution (referendum within six months); seek EU reform, restore Social Chapter opt‑out and national control over fisheries; back enlargement including Turkey. Lead on free trade, the rule of law and property rights; meet 0.7% aid by 2013 with more national control.

Day One: Begin recruiting 5,000 extra police a year; bring back Matron; first Budget to cut waste and lower taxes; empower heads to expel; start 24‑hour port surveillance; set the EU Constitution referendum date.
